items.reasons: Nothing the installed client, the repository or the sources say contradicts either return, so rule 15 does not force 'neither'. A's 'user-typed commands' matches C1/C2, and B's Skill clause matches C3 and R5. B's `/plugin` is missing from the headless command list (C4), but it is a real interactive command (R10), and NF1 finds /plugin dialog fixes at 2.1.247-2.1.280. The current line also scored 10 correct statuses in K5-K6. But it tells the model to use commands the installed client refuses to run for it (C1, C2), so under rule 15 it loses to either return. Between the returns, the preregistered K5-K6 order ranks B first: wrong_status ties at 0, correct_status is B 10 vs A 8, and non_answer ties at 0. The whole gap is in K5 (A '5; 0; 3; 0; 2', B '5; 0; 5; 0; 1'). The hook ran in every run, but two A runs took A's fallback and reported unconfirmed with a negative lean ('nothing in this session suggests it is'). This evidence has limits. The gap is 2 runs of 5. B's five affirmations followed Bash reads, under bypassPermissions, that included the process command line and the fixture's hook state file. Interactive sessions were not tested. On wording, B's 'Distinguish listed availability from successful execution' matches three things: R27 (a tool list can come from the discovery cache before any connection), the K6 fixture (tools stay listed while the server is not connected) and the repository's own check at docs/token-session-handbook.md:67 ('make one useful call and check its returned content'). This is agreement with the sources, not a measured change in behavior, since every arm scored 5 of 5 on K6. B also covers agents, which T1 lists as a plugin component and A omits. B's order, read-only diagnostics first and then asking the user, follows examples/claude-native/CLAUDE.md:17 and the client's own refusal text (C1/C2 'Ask the user to run'). A's best argument is that its fallback still gives a status in headless runs and workflow children (round_2_points). The matching risk for B is untested, not refuted. B never asked the user in any headless run (asks_user 0 in K1-K3, K4 and K5-K6; question_only 0 and non_answer 0 in K5-K6). A is shorter and cost less per run (K5-K6 total USD 1.9892 vs 2.4406, which the packet marks descriptive only). B read settings files in 2 more K6 runs (evidence_settings 7 vs 5). Every arm read them in K5, so this is a minor cost under AGENTS.md:43. Neither point outweighs B's edge in correct statuses or its better-sourced verification standard.
